subject: How to model latent variables for constructs measured by a single item?

messages.author: d54df7841aa15cc4
messages.subject: How to model latent variables for constructs measured by a single item?
parts:
My mediation model has 3 constructs (job satisfaction, supportive behaviour and peceived recognition; one of which (behaviour) is measured as a latent construct with 6 latent factors. The other two were measured using single items.


How do you model latent variables for all 3 constructs? I'm unsure about the correct way to do this when the constructs are measure using a single item? My current model syntax is shown below:


SCTModel2 <- '

RBehF1=~BF1_RAV+BF2_RAV+BF3_RAV+BF4_RAV+BF6_RAV+BF7_RAV

 

 # direct effect

             RaterJobSat ~ c*RBehF1

           # mediator

            RaterReward ~ a*RBehF1

             RaterJobSat ~ b*RaterReward

           # indirect effect (a*b)

             indirect := a*b

           # total effect

             total := c + (a*b)

RBehF1~~RaterJobSat

RBehF1~~RaterReward

RaterReward~~RaterJobSat

'


Thanks,


Emma.

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: How to model latent variables for constructs measured by a single item?
parts: a latent construct with 6 latent factors.
Just to clarify terms, Behavior  is the latent common factor.  It has six observed indicators.  Latent = unobserved.
How do you model latent variables for all 3 constructs? I'm unsure about the correct way to do this when the constructs are measure using a single item?

The same way you specify a construct with more indicators.  Just name the relevant indicators after the "=~" operator.

JobSat =~ RaterJobSat 
Reward =~ RaterReward

If you are using the sem() function, it will automatically add the necessary identification constraints (i.e., fixing the residual variances of the indicators to zero, so that all of their variance is represented in the latent construct).
